2609.00377.title: FoldingAgent: Inferring Parametric Origami Procedures from Demonstration Videos
2609.00377.paper_summary: We present FoldingAgent, an agentic framework for inferring explicit parametric folding programs directly from origami demonstration videos. Our framework leverages the reasoning power of a pre-trained Vision-Language Model (VLM) equipped with a suite of specialized tools that enable the agent to simulate geometric transitions, verify physical plausibility, retrieve and compare visual content, and evaluate its own predictions. To translate visual content into folding programs, we define a parametric space that consists of the paper's geometry and a set of parametric folding actions. Unlike models that predict static crease patterns, our agent operates sequentially and possesses the ability to re-plan its actions, effectively mitigating the compounding errors inherent in multi-step folding. Our approach takes a step toward closing the gap between human origami knowledge, which is primarily shared through unstructured visual demonstrations, and computational methods, which typically rely on structured, parametric representations such as a crease pattern or an executable parametric plan. We evaluate our approach on PurelandFold, a newly curated benchmark of diverse Pureland origami videos with ground-truth geometry and action labels. Our results demonstrate that by combining VLM reasoning with a set of specialized tools and physical simulation, we can successfully transform unstructured visual demonstrations into executable, physically plausible folding procedures.
2609.00377.paper_summary_zh: 我們提出了FoldingAgent，一個能夠直接從摺紙示範影片推斷明確參數摺疊程序的代理框架。<lb/>我們的框架利用了一個預訓練的視覺-語言模型（VLM）的推理能力，並配備了一套專門的工具，使代理能夠模擬幾何過渡、驗證物理合理性、檢索和比較視覺內容，以及評估自身的預測。<lb/>為了將視覺內容轉換為摺疊程序，我們定義了一個參數空間，該空間由紙張的幾何形狀和一組參數摺疊動作組成。<lb/>與預測靜態摺痕模式的模型不同，我們的代理是順序運作的，並且具備重新規劃其行動的能力，有效減少了多步摺疊中固有的累積誤差。<lb/>我們的方法朝著縮小人類摺紙知識與計算方法之間的差距邁出了一步，前者主要通過非結構化的視覺示範共享，而後者通常依賴於結構化的參數表示，如摺痕模式或可執行的參數計畫。<lb/>我們在PurelandFold上評估我們的方法，這是一個新近整理的多樣化Pureland摺紙影片基準，具有真實幾何和動作標籤。<lb/>我們的結果表明，通過將VLM推理與一套專門工具和物理模擬相結合，我們能夠成功地將非結構化的視覺示範轉換為可執行的、物理合理的摺疊程序。
